title: Constructible cospecialization criterion over arbitrary schemes
statement: Let Y be an arbitrary scheme [def-pc-scheme] and Lambda a commutative Noetherian ring. Let G be a constructible sheaf of Lambda-modules on the small etale site of Y [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-constructible-constructible]. For every geometric point s: Spec Omega -> Y and geometric point t: Spec Omega-prime -> Y_(s) of the strict localization, suppose the canonical cospecialization map G_s -> G_(t over Y) is bijective (the strict-localization cospecializationMap convention). Then G is finite locally constant [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant]. No Noetherian hypothesis on Y is imposed.

source.place: Lemma characterize-locally-constant-module, Tag 0GKC: finite-presentation spreading step. The constructible variant replaces the finite-irreducible-components argument by the constructible kernel/cokernel neighborhood argument already proved in lean/WeilConjectures/ConstructibleSheaf/SpecializationCriterion.lean.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point s above y. Constructibility makes the stalk M=G_s a finite module; since the coefficient ring is Noetherian it is finitely presented. The existing finite-presentation colimit API exists_comp_toPresheafFiber_eq_id spreads the identity to an affine pointed etale neighborhood V. The constantSheafSpread morphism psi from the constant M-sheaf to G restricted to V is the identity at s.

The constant M-sheaf and the inverse image of G are constructible. Their morphism psi has constructible kernel and cokernel by the constructible Serre theorem. On the affine scheme V their zero-stalk loci are open in the constructible topology, by the already proved isOpen_constructibleTopology_stalkZeroLocus API.

Every generization of the distinguished point of V lifts to a point of the strict localization at s. The stalk map of psi at that point identifies with the cospecialization map of G, hence is an isomorphism. Thus all these generizations lie in the intersection Z of the two zero-stalk loci. The spectral-space constructible-neighborhood lemma, implemented by exists_isOpen_subset_of_isOpen_constructibleTopology, gives an ordinary open neighborhood of the distinguished point contained in Z. This uses only that V is affine (hence spectral), not that the base is locally Noetherian.

On that open neighborhood the kernel and cokernel have zero stalks, so stalk conservativity makes the restriction of psi an isomorphism. Composing with the constant-sheaf inverse-image comparison gives an etale constant neighborhood of y. Such neighborhoods, one for each y, form an etale cover. The existing finite stalk modules supply IsFiniteSheaf, so the sheaf is finite locally constant.

proof_origin.reason: Generalize the existing source-library constructible-topology proof in WeilConjectures/ConstructibleSheaf/SpecializationCriterion.lean by dropping the unused IsLocallyNoetherian base instance and its unused affine-neighborhood instance. All imported APIs already hold over arbitrary schemes; the generalized Lean proof compiles without holes.

lean.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf_of_constructible_bijective_cospecialization
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) [IsConstructibleSheaf G]
    (hG : ∀ {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) {Ω' : Type u}
      [Field Ω'] [IsSepClosed Ω'] (t : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ strictLocalization s),
      Function.Bijective (cospecializationMap s t (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) G).hom) :
    IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf G
